relations.myth: The dolphin assumes human form to seek a lover
relations.note: Yacuruna may manifest as a dolphin disguised as a human lover or acquaintance.
relations.source: Regan, Hacia la tierra sin mal

relations.note: Sirens are classified as Yacuruna or as transformations within the same aquatic complex.
relations.source: Regan, Hacia la tierra sin mal

relations.note: Regan places the Mother of the Water within the broader Yacuruna transformational class.
relations.source: Regan, Hacia la tierra sin mal

relations.myth: The water person appears as a great boa
relations.note: Yacuruna overlap or transform into great boas understood as water owners or deceased shamans.

relations.myth: Karuara resist Purahua's destructive riverbank erosion
relations.note: Karuara oppose Purahua and protect land threatened by the great water-serpent.
Missionaries classified indigenous aquatic beings as devils within Christian demonology.
